Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: 5/5: Fast, careful, and they caught a mistake in my drawing before cutting

5/5

I want to write a real review and not only "great shop," because I know other labs and the purchasing office read these when they pick vendors.

**What we ordered**

I'm a postdoc in the Ostrowski group. We needed two parts for our near-IR camera before our Palomar run on November 18:

- a camera-to-dewar adapter plate
- a light baffle tube with internal threads

Both are 6061-T6 and black anodized (PO 26-41187). The schedule was very tight. One large vendor quoted us 6 weeks, which would have missed the run completely. Arroyo quoted 21 days, including a rush setup fee, so we went with them.

**They actually read the drawing**

This is the main reason I'm writing. Before cutting the plate, Ruben emailed me because Tiff, who was doing the setup, noticed something strange. Every dimension on the drawing was in mm except the bolt circle, which said 4.125. If they had cut it at 4.125 mm, the screw holes would have landed inside the bore and the plate would be useless. The value was supposed to be 4.125 inches (104.8 mm).

To be honest, this was completely my fault. I copied the number from the old drawing for our previous camera and never converted it. Many shops would just machine exactly what is on the paper. Then I would have a beautiful, perfectly anodized plate that doesn't fit anything, a week before the telescope run. Tiff stopped and asked instead. That shows me the people at Arroyo think about what the part is for, not only what the numbers say. Thank you, Tiff.

**Quality (from our fit test on 11/9)**

- All 8 screws went into the dewar without any forcing.
- Flatness across the plate face was under 0.01 mm on the dial indicator.
- Baffle threads were smooth.
- No light leak in our dark test: lab lights on, 300 s dark frame, and the result looked the same as with the dewar closed. For an IR camera this matters a lot.
- Anodize is even, with no bare spots, inside and outside.
- They sent an inspection sheet with the parts.

**Speed**

Quoted lead time was 21 days. Actual time from PO to delivery was **9 days**, including the outside anodizing. Ruben also drove the parts to the Robinson loading dock himself on his way to another supplier, and he didn't charge for delivery. I was so happy to see them I almost hugged him.

**Communication**

Ruben answers emails clearly, asks questions when something is unclear, and tells you exactly when the parts will be ready. When you are trying to make a telescope date, this is just as important as the machining.

**For purchasing and other labs**

I know there is a question about why we don't always use the big vendor. In our case the big vendor would have been 6 weeks and we would have lost the run. Arroyo was more than 4x faster, the quality was excellent, and they caught a drawing error that would have cost us the whole order. I would strongly recommend adding Arroyo Precision Works to the preferred vendor list. Our group will definitely use them again, and I think any lab doing precision or prototype parts (instrument mounts, optical hardware, small vacuum parts) should give them a try.

Thank you Ruben, Tiff, and everyone at Arroyo. Our camera is going to Palomar on time because of you.

Lin Wei, Ostrowski group (Astrophysics)
